DILG BAGONG PILIPINAS Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA cor. Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City www.dilg.gov.ph OPINION NO. S. MR. BRANDON L. LEE Internal Auditor, Internal Audit Division National Kidney and Transplant Institute Dear Mr. Lee: This has reference to your letter dated February 15, 2024, requesting this Department's legal opinion concerning the local ordinances of Negros Occidental and Bacolod City. Per your representation, Provincial Ordinance No. 2019-24, Series of 2019 of Negros Occidental and Negros Occidental, Bacolod City Joint Executive Order No. 1, Series of 2003 are against National Policies, such as: (I) Department of Agriculture Circular No. 2, Series of 2022; (2) Department of the Interior and Local Government Memorandum Circular No. 2021-006; and (2) Office of the President Administrative Order No. 22, Series of 2020. The said National policies allows the transport of processed pork products between 2 RED infected zones. However, the subject ordinance and executive order are inconsistent with the said national policies as they do not allow transport of processed pork within the local government's jurisdiction. Further, you alleged that the province allows entry of processed pork products coming from a manufacturer based in Mandaue City, the reason of the local government is that — their pork supply originates from Italy. Hence, the instant request for assistance/legal opinion from the Department. At the outset, the Department agrees with you that for an ordinance to be valid, it must not only be within the corporate powers of the LGU to enact and must be passed according to the procedure prescribed by law, it must also conform to the following substantive requirements: Must not contravene the Constitution or any Statute; (2) Must not be unfair or oppressive; (3) Must not be partial or discriminatory; (4) Must not prohibit but may regulate trade; (5) Must be general and consistent with public policy; and (6) Must not be unreasonable However, it is with regret to inform you that this Department is an agency under the executive branch of the government, and as such, it is devoid of authority to declare invalid or illegal any ordinance/executive order enacted by the LGUs. "Matino, Mahusay at Maaasahan" Trunkline No. (02) 8876 3454

The Department, in its previous legal opinions have already opined that inasmuch as the procedural process for its enactment complies with the provisions of the Local Government Code, the same is considered valid unless declared otherwise by our courts of justice. Any issues or questions thereon as to the substantive validity and enforceability of an ordinance should be threshed out by filing a special civil action for declaratory relief before the proper court in accordance with Sections I and 4, Rule 63 of the Revised Rules of Court, to wit: Section 1. Who may file petition. — Any person interested under a deed, will, contract or other written instrument, or whose rights are affected by a statute, executive order or regulation, ordinance, or any other governmental regulation may, before breach or violation thereof bring an action in the appropriate Regional Trial Court to determine any question of construction or validity arising, and for a declaration of his rights or duties, thereunder. An action for the reformation of an instrument, to quiet title to real property or remove clouds therefrom, or to consolidate ownership under Article 1607 of the Civil Code, may be brought under this Rule. Section 4. Local government ordinances. — In any action involving the validity of a local government ordinance, the corresponding prosecutor or attorney of the local governmental unit involved shall be similarly notified and entitled to be heard. If such ordinance is alleged to be unconstitutional, the Solicitor General shall also be notified and entitled to be heard. This opinion shall be without prejudice to any contrary opinion rendered by more competent authorities and/or the courts. We hope to have guided you on the matter. Thank you.
